bull_case_summary: Maybank offers an income thesis at 11.51x trailing earnings and a reported 6.2% yield, supported by broadly stable profit and quantified CET1 of 15.657%. Round two retains the proposed dividend deduction and argues that disclosed capital and limited net-impairment movement provide risk compensation without requiring rapid growth.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts a credible income purchase but notes falling operating income, gross impaired loans rising to RM9.362bn and declining capital ratios before dividend deduction. Round two narrows opposition to aggressive buying under these observed trends rather than missing capital evidence.
key_points_of_agreement: Disclosed capital provides a measured cushion.
Profit resilience is not earnings acceleration.
Yield is conditional income, not guaranteed total return.
key_points_of_disagreement: How far capital and 6.2% income compensate simultaneous operating-income and gross-credit deterioration.
unresolved_uncertainties: Post-dividend capital and future credit-loss trajectory.
Persistence of distributable income if cost restraint cannot offset revenue erosion.
